name: Slashdot

sources.title: Slashdot homepage — live 'News for nerds' with user account login; stories credited to submitters
Slashdot Software directory — B2B software comparisons; 'Add Your Software' links to the SourceForge vendor flow at /software/vendors/new

requirements: Two distinct surfaces: (1) the news site — users submit story links for editor selection at slashdot.org/submission (requires a free account); (2) the software directory — vendors add products via the 'Add Your Software' link which routes into the SourceForge/Slashdot Media vendor flow
Story submissions are free but editors choose what runs — 'News for nerds' tech/science angle required
Directory listings are for business software vendors; submission happens on the SourceForge side of the shared platform
slashdot.org/submission blocked automated fetch (403) — historically the submit-story form requiring login
preparation: For news: a Slashdot account plus a genuinely interesting tech/science story link with a neutral summary
For the software directory: vendor details for the SourceForge vendor form (the 'Add Your Software' link jumps to the SourceForge-side vendor signup)
workflow: News route: create a Slashdot account, open slashdot.org/submission, submit the story link + summary; editors decide
Directory route: from slashdot.org/software/, click 'Add Your Software' and complete the vendor listing flow on the SourceForge platform
Directory listing, once live, appears at slashdot.org/software/p/<product>/ with ratings/reviews
Paid option: 'Software Advertising Options' link on the software page for sponsored placement
watchFor: The news site and software directory are different products — don't confuse a story submission with a vendor listing
Catalog source lists slashdot.org over plain HTTP — use HTTPS
Slashdot Media shares the SourceForge back end — vendor onboarding may land you on sourceforge.net pages
Sponsored listings sort above organic ones in the directory ('Sponsored' sort default)
Story acceptance is at editor discretion — most submissions are rejected
countsAsLive: News: a submitted story is published on the Slashdot front page. Directory: the product appears at slashdot.org/software/p/<name>/
unknowns: Whether the vendor listing flow is free or paid for basic listings — the pricing page lives behind the transfer link
Editorial acceptance rate for story submissions
